metadata.title: Miami & Dade County Historical GIS Data Source Index
metadata.description: Priority-ranked index of data sources for building a historical GIS of Miami and Dade County, 1910-1930
metadata.project: Built by Labor, Divided by Design

sources.name: NHGIS County Boundaries and Aggregate Data
sources.notes: Boundary shapefiles automatically reflect Palm Beach split (1909) and Broward split (1915). Includes population tables by race, nativity, sex, age, occupation.

sources.name: Mapping Inequality (HOLC Redlining)
sources.notes: Includes both vector polygons AND georeferenced scan of original HOLC map as GeoTIFF. Area descriptions contain qualitative racial assessments by HOLC surveyors.

sources.name: USGS topoView (Historical Topographic Maps)
sources.notes: Pre-georeferenced GeoTIFFs. Click Miami area in viewer, filter to 1:62,500 scale for pre-1930 maps.
download_steps: Click tile to see available editions

sources.name: Library of Congress Sanborn Maps - Miami
sources.coverage: City of Miami + Miami Beach + Coconut Grove
sources.license: Public domain (pre-1923 definitely; LOC has digitized all)

editions.notes: MOST COMPREHENSIVE - Volume 1 with skeleton maps
Vols 2-3: Miami Beach, Coral Gables, Silver Bluff

sources.notes: Must georeference in QGIS using Miami-Dade parcel data as control. Budget 2-4 hours per sheet. ProQuest Sanborn Maps Geo Edition has pre-georeferenced GeoTIFFs but requires institutional subscription.

sources.name: Miami-Dade County GIS Open Data Portal
sources.notes: Current parcel layer useful for georeferencing historical Sanborn maps. Historic sites and districts layers available.

sources.name: City of Miami GIS Open Data
sources.notes: Historic Districts layer includes designated historic structures from the study era.

sources.name: NOAA Historical Hurricane Tracks
sources.notes: HURDAT2 is the raw CSV. The interactive viewer lets you export custom shapefiles.

sources.name: IPUMS USA Full-Count Census Microdata
key_variables: ENUMDIST (enumeration district - links to ED maps)

sources.name: FIU Historical Aerial Photographs (USCGS 1927)
sources.notes: Invaluable for mapping extent of 1920s development and artificial islands. 1927 coverage is best.

sources.name: Florida Geographic Data Library
sources.notes: Good source for modern basemap layers: parcels, hydrography, transportation.

sources.name: Old Maps Online - Miami
sources.notes: Aggregator linking to LOC, Rumsey, and other sources. Set date slider to 1900-1930.

sources.name: David Rumsey Map Collection
sources.notes: Built-in Georeferencer tool for unreferenced maps. Search 'Miami' or 'Dade County' with date filter.

sources.name: OpenHistoricalMap
sources.notes: Crowd-sourced historical OSM. Coverage for 1920s Miami likely sparse but viewable with date slider. Could be contributed to as part of this project.

sources.name: LOC 1925 Map of Miami (Sauer & Seghy)
sources.notes: 'Map of the city of Miami and environs' by Sauer & Seghy. Useful for boom-era city extent. Requires georeferencing.

sources.name: Florida Memory (State Archives of Florida)
sources.notes: 300+ digitized FL maps including township, highway, railroad. WPA Church Records list 200+ Dade County churches. Requires georeferencing.

sources.name: FamilySearch Enumeration District Maps
sources.notes: Scanned ED maps from NARA Microfilm A3378. Search 'Enumeration District Maps, Dade County, Florida' for 1910, 1920, 1930. Must georeference and digitize as polygons.

sources.name: UMiami Libraries Digital Collections
sources.notes: Purdy, Tebeau, and Douglas map subcollections. Overtown Oral History Project has geographic references. Race and Property StoryMap documents deed restrictions.

sources.name: FIU Miami Metropolitan Archive
sources.notes: Early city council minutes, urban planning documents, charters. Best source for reconstructing historical City of Miami boundaries from annexation ordinances.

sources.name: HistoryMiami Museum Archives
sources.notes: 1,900+ maps; 1M+ photos; Romer Collection (1925-1950s). Most access is in-person. Essential for deep research.

sources.name: Miami-Dade County Clerk's Official Records
sources.notes: Historical plat maps, deed records with racial covenants, annexation ordinances. Free search but requires manual document mining.

academic_sources.citation: Paul S. George, 'Colored Town: Miami's Black Community, 1896-1930' (Florida Historical Quarterly, 1977)
academic_sources.relevance: Definitive article on Overtown geography and development

academic_sources.citation: N.D.B. Connolly, 'A World More Concrete' (U of Chicago Press, 2014)
academic_sources.relevance: Race, real estate, and Jim Crow South Florida; co-led Mapping Inequality project

academic_sources.citation: Marvin Dunn, 'Black Miami in the Twentieth Century' (UPF, 1997)
academic_sources.relevance: Definitive history of Black Miami; racial violence, settlements
Housing discrimination, I-95 destruction of Overtown

academic_sources.citation: David Chalmers, 'The Ku Klux Klan in the Sunshine State: The 1920s' (FHQ, 1963)
Raymond A. Mohl, 'Black Immigrants: Bahamians in Early Twentieth-Century Miami' (FHQ, 1986)

gaps_and_known_issues.approach: Download NARA scanned ED maps from FamilySearch, georeference in QGIS against modern Miami-Dade parcel layer, digitize polygons, join to IPUMS ENUMDIST variable

gaps_and_known_issues.gap: Historical City of Miami annexation boundaries
gaps_and_known_issues.approach: Mine FIU Miami Metropolitan Archive for annexation ordinances; trace from historical plat maps; create shapefile per year (1896, 1913, 1920, 1925)

gaps_and_known_issues.effort: MEDIUM (2-4 hrs per sheet; ~500 hours for full 1921 set)
gaps_and_known_issues.approach: Use QGIS Georeferencer with Miami-Dade parcel data as control. Prioritize 1921 edition (123 sheets). Check ProQuest Sanborn Geo Edition via institutional subscription.
Cross-reference georeferenced Sanborn maps (1914, 1918, 1921), ED maps, and Paul George's scholarship to refine the approximate polygons in boundaries.geojson
Mine Miami-Dade Clerk's deed records by subdivision; UMiami Race and Property StoryMap has partial coverage
Use Tundria 1928 map overlay (http://www.tundria.com/trams/USA/Miami-1928.php) as digitizing guide

gaps_and_known_issues.gap: Pre-1920 Black school and church locations
gaps_and_known_issues.approach: Florida Memory WPA Church Records (200+ Dade County churches); Miami-Dade Public Schools historical records
USGS topoview land-cover on 1915 topo; 1927 FIU aerials for extent mapping
